evals/tier3/prompts/arm_c.md + the runner's cooperation path - the typed check (D50 (4)). Stage 2 returns CooperationCheckVerdict: concur (bool), objections (a list of strings, non-empty when concur is false), requested as JSON through the client's response_format handling. Stage 3 runs only when concur is false (the objections inlined into the revision call). A check that answers in any other shape is not a verdict: after the bounded retries it is recorded 'unavailable' and model 1's draft is delivered - never a concurrence, never a refusal to deliver; when the retries spend the last call, the starvation is recorded ('starved') and the draft is delivered with the objection beside it. Each stage is a separate call that shows the model only its own stage's text, the question, and the inputs that stage names. No voting, no third model, and no control flow that reads prose (hard rule 2).

The arm B tools (D50 (5)) - fetch_primary_source and recompute, both deterministic, both recorded. fetch_primary_source(citation) accepts a CFR citation in the forms the questions write it ('29 CFR § 1910.146(b)', '40 CFR 141.62(b)', with or without '§' and the paragraph), normalises to title and section, and returns that section's July 1, 2014 edition text from evals/tier2/sources/ (the committed .txt; the largest, 1910.146, is 157,342 bytes). Any other citation gets a typed not-available result - recorded, not a refusal - and the tool opens no socket (the suite's hermetic network guard is the proof: the closed-world fetch tests run with 0 non-loopback attempts). recompute(expression) evaluates arithmetic by walking a whitelisted syntax tree: numbers, + - × ÷ and powers, parentheses, pi, e, and sqrt, exp, ln, log10, sin, cos, tan, their inverses, abs, min and max. It never evals, execs or compiles model text (hard rule 3); names, attributes, calls outside the whitelist, keyword arguments, non-numeric arguments, string and boolean constants, and oversized exponents and results all return typed rejections the model reads as the answer to its request. The loop's structure is registered: at most 3 model calls and 20 tool invocations per unit; calls 1 and 2 offer the tools, call 3 offers none (the model must answer); each round's tool results are inlined into the next call's user message; every invocation is recorded (the tool, its arguments, the result's size, any error).

Every model call in arms A-D carries max_tokens 8000 and temperature 0.3 (the client's default; 8000 is more than 3x the largest completion 107's direct calls used); finish_reason is recorded per call and a truncated answer is scored as delivered and flagged; arm E runs on the pipeline's own standing caps. A TIER3 pin names its serving the way a MODEL_* tier does, with the same per-tier provider-preference syntax under the arm's name, and the runner records every call's resolved model and provider. Quoted per tier, at the guard's own formula (openrouter.py _guard_spend: (prompt bytes + 512) x the prompt rate + max_tokens x the completion rate) and the catalogue's rates (free public GET), against the $0.50 per-unit ceiling: arm E/triage (google/gemini-3.8-flash) - no worst case the guard can bound: carries charges beside prompt and completion tokens (audio, image, input_audio_cache, input_cache_read, input_cache_write, internal_reasoning, web_search), which a token-only worst case understates; arm E/research (google/gemini-3.8-flash) - the same; arm E/search (perplexity/sonar) - no worst case the guard can bound: carries charges beside prompt and completion tokens (web_search); arm E/architecture (xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-pro:exacto) - no worst case the guard can bound: served but not priced in the catalogue (confirmed via the per-model endpoint); arm E/engineering (qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507) - no worst case the guard can bound: carries charges beside prompt and completion tokens (input_cache_read); arm E/judge (moonshotai/kimi-k2.5:exacto) - served but not priced in the catalogue; arm E/escalation (moonshotai/kimi-k3:exacto) - served but not priced in the catalogue.
